agree.reason: A wary reader who has quit before will find the candid A1C hedge, low-risk $59 week, no-contract plan and offer of a call with the dietitian credible enough to try one week, though nothing speaks directly to why this would last when the earlier tries did not.

honest.reason: It drops the 'will lower your A1C' promise and is open about the one customer who went up, but it pins the 0.6-point average drop on the ten whose A1C fell when the brief gives it as an overall average, it calls the call 'free' though the brief never says so, and it leaves out that medication changes were not tracked.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are mostly repeated as given, with no per-meal cost ($5.90 for the trial, $12.90 on the plan), no 10-of-14 shown as about 7 in 10, and no 37-of-88 shown as a share that stays past six months.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative described is the work of planning and counting carbs yourself, and the page never sets itself against the apps and delivery services this reader has already tried and quit.

qualification.reason: The A1C hedge is honest and names a real uncertainty, but it gives the reader nothing to check, such as retesting A1C after three months with their doctor and cancelling if it hasn't moved.

objections.reason: Swaps, a 4-week menu cycle, no contract and the 37 customers past six months quietly answer the 'I'll get bored and quit' worry, but the page never names that worry or the reader's past dropouts outright.

fit.reason: It is a clear, well-sectioned sales page close to the requested 400 words, ending on the trial-week order button the client wanted.
